caseno: Civil Appeal No. 6 of 1975 from Civil Revision No. 127 of 1969.
lawyer: M.H. Khandokar, Senior Advocate instructed by S. M. Huq, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellant. S.R. Pal, Senior Advocate, instructed by Abdur Rab II. Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Syed Ahmed Molla ------ Appellant
Vs. 
Halima Begum and others  ------ Respondent.
full_judgment: 5. Mr. M. H. Khondker, learned Counsel for the appellant in support of the appeal submitted that the lands in C. S. plot Nos. 1202 and 1203 along with six other plots (1204 to 1209 were recorded in C. S. Khatian No. 39 of mouza Debnagar, P.S Daulatpur, District Khulna in the name of Ujiruddin Nayan Shaikh and Abdus Samad Shaikh in equal shares as under raiytas with right of occupancy under the raiyati recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 38 of the said mouza. The said two plots namely, 1202 and 1203, were recorded in possession of Abdus Sarnad and the said C. S. Khatinus were finally published on 13.5.1927. Delwar Shaikh alias Delwar Hosszin alias Dolwar Ahmed, brother of the recorded tenant Abdus Samad and husband of Sakhina alias Rokeya or Salhina or Rabeya, was in possession of the aforesaid lands and being in such possession claimed the land to be his and sold the same along with some other lands to the appellant in consideration by a registered kabala dated 21.4.1951, and put the appellant in possession thereof, and since then the appellant has been in peaceful possession by making certain pucca constructions, and on payment of rents along with his co-sharer tenants to the landlord and thereafter to the Government after the acquisition of the Rent-receiving interest by the Government Preparation of record of rights was started under the provisions of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the aforesaid two plots had been corded in the preliminary stage in the name of Sultan Shaikh, son of late Nayan Shaikh. The appellant fled objection for correction of record on 1.8.60 making the said Delwar Shaikh as preform defendant thereto and asserted that he has been in possession of the said two plots of land, 1202 and 1203, by purchase from Delwar Shaikh. The Assistant Settlement Officer by the judgment and order dated 29.8.60 recorded the appellant's name after striking out of the name of Sultan Shaikh. Thereafter record of rights (being khatian No. 34) under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been prepared and finally published in the name of the appellant and the other co-sharer tenant, Abdus Sabur Khan, who acquired the other two plots of land from the heirs of the said two c-sharer tenants, namely, Ujir Shaikh and Nayan Shaikh. It appears that the aforesaid plots of lands were not included in the said Kabala dated 21.4.51 on the basis of which the appellant claimed to be co-sharer. At this the said Delwar Hossain gave another kabala in respect of the said lands executed by his wife named Rokeya and made over a deed of relinquishment dated 1.5.36 in the name of his wife Sakhina Khatun executed by his brother, Abdus Samad Shaikh. The appellant remained in peaceful possession since 21.4.51 and neither Delwar Hossain nor Sakhina nor Rokeya nor anybody else had possessed the same, so the appellant is a co-share tenant in the holding recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 39, now S. A. Katina No. 34, While the appellant and the said Khan Brothers were the recorded co-sharer tenants in the holding, the co-sharer Khalil Brothers sold their share by a registered kabala dated 3.12.66 to a stranger, Md. Khalilur Rahman, Respondent No. 4, for consideration of Taka 6,000.00. The appellant was served with the notice of this transfer on 8.12.66 and thereupon he made an application for preemption as stated earlier.
